scope: Project selection and durable local repository binding; simulated tool results are fixtures, not live integration evidence.

evals.name: single-unrelated-project
evals.prompt: In repo billing-client, user says '/my-architect:init, set this up quickly'. No local binding. list_projects succeeds with exactly [{path:'analytics-platform',name:'Analytics platform'}]. Real test and CI commands are known.
assertions: Offers the returned project or creation of a new one; waits for selection before writing a binding.
Does not infer identity from the only result, result order, or repository name.

evals.name: creation-already-authorized
evals.prompt: User says 'Create a new Architect project for this repo and connect it; use simple hierarchy, name Billing Client.' No binding. list_projects succeeds with an empty list. Real test and CI commands are known.
assertions: Uses the already authorized name and preset without repeated permission questions.
Calls scaffold_project with withSampleContent:false; obtains the exact ID from the successful response, verifies it, and persists the local binding.
Does not invent requirements or report complete traceability for a new empty project.

evals.name: confirmed-binding
evals.prompt: User says '/my-architect:init'. CLAUDE.md has my_architect pid: "Billing Client"; .architect/traceability.json has the same projectId. MCP access succeeds. Real test and CI commands are known.
assertions: Reuses the exact ID, including spaces, with no new identity question or project creation.
Preserves the binding while inspecting and repairing actual traceability gaps.

evals.name: list-failure-is-not-empty
evals.prompt: User says '/my-architect:init'. No local binding. list_projects returns an authentication error. Real test and CI commands are known.
assertions: Reports a connection/authentication problem, not zero projects.
Does not scaffold, persist an invented binding, or claim successful setup.

evals.name: conflicting-bindings
evals.prompt: User says '/my-architect:init'. .architect/traceability.json projectId is Alpha; CLAUDE.md explicitly says my_architect pid: "Beta". Real test and CI commands are known.
assertions: Shows the two conflicting IDs and asks which is correct before dependent writes.
Preserves the existing index and bindings while resolution is pending.

evals.name: selected-project-survives-restart
evals.prompt: No initial binding. list_projects returns Alpha and Billing Client (exact path 'billing client / europe'). The user chooses Billing Client. get_project_context succeeds. Real test and CI commands are known. Describe what survives a fresh session and what you do on the next /my-architect:init.
assertions: Persists the returned path exactly in local config/instructions, rather than relying on conversational memory or slugifying it.
The next session reuses the saved binding without asking again.
Describes a local pointer, not a server-side Git repository integration.

evals.name: new-project-choice-and-empty-requirements
evals.prompt: User says '/my-architect:init'. There is no binding; list_projects succeeds with no projects. The user has not supplied a name or hierarchy preference. After answering your necessary questions, they authorize creating an empty project. Its requirements export is empty.
assertions: Explains creation and asks for the missing project name/hierarchy choice before scaffold.
Creates no sample content; saves a returned and verified ID.
Reports that linking succeeded but traceability remains incomplete until real requirements/tests/CI are present.

evals.name: custom-levels-are-not-a-scaffold-argument
evals.prompt: User requests a new custom hierarchy Product → Slice. The live scaffold_project schema accepts preset but has no levelNames argument. No project has been created or linked.
assertions: Explains that preset:custom does not pass arbitrary level names through scaffold_project.
Does not invent a levelNames argument or substitute default levels while claiming the requested hierarchy exists.
Resolves a supported way to configure those levels before dependent creation/binding claims.
